scope: Sixteen finite failglob contexts with original GNU diagnostics and status comparisons; full child memory tracing. File fixtures contain two ordinary matches in each of two directories.

results.name: literal-prefix
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
printf "%s\n" "two words" absent*
printf "after\n"

results.name: remaining-words
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
printf "%s\n" absent* "tail words" file_a
printf "after\n"

results.name: one-match
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
printf "%s\n" file_a* absent*
printf "after\n"

results.name: multiple-matches
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
printf "%s\n" file_* absent* tail
printf "after\n"

results.name: two-patterns
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
printf "%s\n" file_* dir/* absent* tail
printf "after\n"

results.name: brace-patterns
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
printf "%s\n" {file_*,dir/*} absent* tail
printf "after\n"

results.name: nullglob-precedence
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
shopt -s nullglob
printf "%s\n" file_* absent*
printf "after\n"

results.name: function
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
f() { printf "%s\n" file_* absent* tail; }
f
printf "after\n"

results.name: subshell
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
( printf "%s\n" file_* absent* tail )
printf "after\n"

results.name: substitution
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
result=$(printf "%s\n" file_* absent* tail)
printf "result:<%s>\n" "$result"
printf "after\n"

results.name: group
temporary-assignment
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
VALUE=example printf "%s\n" file_* absent* tail
printf "after\n"

results.name: eval
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
eval 'printf "%s\n" file_* absent* tail'
printf "after\n"

results.name: exit-trap
results.script:
shopt -s failglob
trap 'printf "exit:%s\n" "$?"' EXIT
printf '%s\n' file_* absent* tail
printf "after\n"
